headline: Computational RNA modeling spans binding-site search, inverse folding, and AlphaFold3 gaps
label: Biomolecular Structure Modeling Foundations
summary: Recent benchmarks of AlphaFold3 and new RNA-targeting methods expose uneven performance and training-data dependence across application areas.
synthesis: The dominant thread is RNA as a structural target for computational modeling, spanning ligand-binding site detection, pseudoknot-aware inverse folding, and drug design. Ribo-LENS applies geometric deep learning to search base-pairing subgraphs for RNA small-molecule binding sites and is reported to outperform AlphaFold3 and Chai-1. PKProbDesign is a sampling-based inverse-folding method that optimizes thermodynamic folding probability for pseudoknotted targets and is reported to outperform DesiRNA. A separate evaluation of AlphaFold3 across ubiquitinated proteins, TCR-epitope, antibody-antigen, protein-RNA and protein-lipid tasks finds uneven performance and training-data dependence. The published review of machine learning for RNA-targeting drug design proposes evaluation standards and benchmarks models on drug-RNA interaction prediction. Together these works suggest that RNA-focused methods are being assessed against general-purpose structure predictors, with evaluation standards becoming a central concern.
